limits.value: the page does not state a port speed

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order; the calculator and licensing pages were read, the checkout was not

confidence_note: every component price is printed on the pricing page, and the vendor's own formula reproduces its three printed presets to the cent. The USD 83.00 total is arithmetic, not a printed plan price, and the checkout was not read.

evidence.proved: the price table lists 4 vCPU Type A at USD 12.00, 16 GiB at USD 42.00, 50 GiB NVMe at USD 10.00 and 5 TB of traffic at USD 0.00
quoted: 'Microsoft Windows Server - Any Version, Any Edition | Per Server | $10 / $19'
the page's calculation formula reproduces the three printed presets USD 4.00 (1 vCPU/1 GiB/20 GiB), USD 25.00 (2 vCPU/2 GiB/20 GiB) and USD 39.00 (2 vCPU/4 GiB/20 GiB)

notes: The total is derived: USD 12.00 CPU + USD 42.00 RAM + USD 10.00 disk + USD 0.00 traffic + USD 19.00 Windows = USD 83.00. A Type B 4-core machine is USD 35.00 and a Type D dedicated 4-core is USD 205.00, so the Type A row is the cheap general-purpose one and its CPU is shared.
